claims.text: Oslo II (28 Sep 1995) divided the West Bank: Area A full PA civil and security control; Area B PA civil and joint security control; Area C full Israeli civil and security control, defined as areas outside A and B; initially A about 3%, B 23–25%, C 72–74%; further redeployments were to transfer part of C by the end of 1999; Wye (1998) called for 13% more, which would have left C at about 61%, but Israel withdrew from only 2%; as of 2013 A about 18%, B 22%, C about 63%; A and B are divided into 165 enclaves without territorial contiguity; about 2.8 million Palestinians in A and B; about 300,000 Palestinians in C (UN).

Less than one per cent of Area C is covered by an approved planning scheme for Palestinian communities; settlement outline plans cover at least 8.5%; of 109 Palestinian outline plans submitted, five were approved; 2009–2018 only 2% of Palestinian building permit requests in Area C were granted (98 of 4,422); 1988–2014 the Civil Administration issued over 14,000 demolition orders.

The Sasson report (March 2005) estimated 105 unauthorized outposts, found the government funded at least part of them, the housing ministry supplied hundreds of mobile homes and millions of dollars, and 54 were built on private Palestinian land without enforcement; Sharon's spokesman blamed overlapping legal codes; the government said its policy was not to establish new settlements.

In February 1994 a settler from Kiryat Arba killed 29 Muslims at the Cave of the Patriarchs; Israel then closed Shuhada Street to Palestinians and closed 304 shops and warehouses; in the 1997 Hebron Protocol Israel agreed to reopen the street; it remains closed to Palestinian shops and vehicles; a 2007 B'Tselem survey found 42% of Palestinians in the H2 city centre (1,014 families) had left; Israel cites protection of settlers.

COGAT (Sep 2015) said OCHA's figures 'are inconsistent with the situation on the ground', that under the interim agreements construction in Area C requires approval from the responsible authorities, that the Civil Administration was processing 13 Palestinian master plans (four completed), and that it was promoting a plan with infrastructure for Bedouin living in unauthorized housing.
